newsitem.title: USA: Natgas futures end up on pre-weekend short cover.
newsitem.headline: Natgas futures end up on pre-weekend short cover.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natural gas futures, helped by some pre-weekend short covering, ended with modest gains Friday, but trade remained light amid little conviction about the market's next move, sources said.
November climbed 4.4 cents to close at $2.181 per million British thermal units. December settled 2.5 cents higher at $2.355. Others ended up by 0.7 to 2.8 cents.

"From a value point of view, the (futures) spread to cash may be a little bearish, but seasonal expectations are bullish," said one Houston-based trader, referring to the approach of winter and better demand.

Technical traders viewed November's close above $2.18 Friday as constructive and likely to lead to a test of the recent high of $2.305, particularly if there is some upside follow-through Monday. Some also noted that the November chart pattern suggested a head-and-shoulders bottom was in place.
But most agreed the market was waiting for clearer direction from the cash when October flows begin Tuesday.
Chartists still pegged November support in the $2.00 area.

Cash sources said weekend Gulf Coast prices skidded more than a dime to the low-$1.80s. October Gulf Coast gas notionally was talked steady to up slightly in the mid-$1.80s. October Midcon was little changed in the low-to-mid $1.70s. New York city gate gas for October delivery again firmed a few cents to near the $2.20 level.
The 12-month Henry Hub strip rose 2.5 cents to $2.11. NYMEX said 18,911 contracts traded, down from Thursday's revised tally of 25,639.
NYMEX November Alberta natgas, in its debut session, settled at 99.0 cents after trading between 98.1 cents and $1.00.
NYMEX Permian natgas was untraded Friday, but November finished four cents higher at $1.82.
On the KCBT, November settled up five cents at $1.94, while deferreds ended one to 5.5 cents higher. The November East/West spread narrowed by 0.6 cent to 24.1 cents (NYMEX premium).
